findings: Retains independent controller and actor references plus exact original struct file custody; no file private_data replacement or struct file layout change.
Generation saturates at signed64 maximum; a lease binds at most one disk and each target binds one OFD for its entire lifetime, including after authorization release.
Lease has only FENCED and REVOKED states. Every marked disk/file/BDI gate denies even a matching actor and exact OFD. Custody observation grants no syscall or I/O permission.
Association spinlock is released before sleepable final fput/target/actor release. A retained real block file pins native disk lifetime; target marker is removed only by final native disk_release.

Fresh-target attach additionally requires exclusive kernel construction ownership and checks unpublished empty disk, no openers/partitions, no capacity/pagecache/device number, and no registered BDI/queue. These preconditions are not inferred from a userspace path.
BDI uses a permanent closed boolean rather than a target pointer, preserving denial when BDI writeback references outlive disk release.
Publication gates cover add_disk, direct bdev inode publication, queue and BDI registration, plus partition creation and rescan.
Operation gates cover native/compat ioctl, io_uring commands, read/write/seek/sync/mmap/fallocate/splice, BIO submission routes, loop queue operations and queue/BDI mutation entries.
Normal disks keep null target and false BDI marker; CONFIG disabled stubs return zero. Coherent full kernel build remains required because disk and BDI layouts change.
remaining_requirements: Actual complete matching object results are pending and do not replace full kernel link or execution.
K1 allocator and control API, K2 native probe/configuration and I/O graph authorization, and K3 lifetime/race/teardown coverage are still required before gates can admit a private device.
Original apexd same-OFD native probe, source admission, Android startup, original-data continuity and application acceptance remain unqualified.
